author: a. j. zhao
title: Adriano Dzhenev receives first Big West Player of the Week honor
text:
University of Hawai’i men’s tennis player Adriano Dzhenev was named Big West Player of the Week after his performances against UC Santa Barbara and Cal Poly, according to an April 1 announcement. This is the sophomore’s first time receiving the weekly conference award, and he becomes the third Rainbow Warrior to earn this recognition during the season.
The award highlights Dzhenev’s recent achievements in both singles and doubles play. He joins teammates Azuma Visaya, who received the honor on January 14, and Timothy Li, who was recognized on February 18.
In doubles matches, Dzhenev partnered with Kent Mueller to secure a key victory against UC Santa Barbara by defeating Diogo Morais and Lorenzo Brunkow with a score of 6-4 on Court #3. Later in the week against Cal Poly, Dzhenev and Mueller played at No. 2 doubles for the first time this season. They were leading their match when it was left unfinished due to another court clinching the doubles point.
Dzhenev also competed in singles matches that went unfinished but showed resilience throughout. Against UCSB’s Miguel Avendano at No. 4 singles, he came back from losing the first set to force a third set before play ended tied at three games each in the final frame. Facing Raz Haviv from Cal Poly at No. 3 singles for his debut at that position this season, Dzhenev won his opening set but split sets before holding a lead when overall team play concluded.
Dzhenev’s consistent performance adds depth to Hawai’i’s lineup as they continue through their tennis schedule.
